title: African Investigative Journalism Conference (AIJC) Fellowship for Francophone Journalists
description: A fully funded fellowship to attend the 2026 African Investigative Journalism Conference (AIJC), the largest annual gathering of African investigative journalists, held November 10-12, 2026 at the Edge Convention Centre in Nairobi, Kenya. Organized by the Wits Centre for Journalism at the University of the Witwatersrand, the conference brings journalists together for lectures, workshops, masterclasses, and seminars on investigative reporting. This fellowship track is specifically for French-speaking (Francophone) investigative journalists and media professionals -- fluency in French, not English, is the operative language requirement, since sessions and materials for this track are conducted in French. Coverage includes return flights from the fellow's home country, ground transport/shuttles, accommodation, conference registration fees, and meals during the conference; no cash stipend is disclosed beyond these covered costs. Open to French-speaking investigative journalists and media professionals (including freelancers) from Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Cote d'Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Guinea, Madagascar, Mali, Niger, Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, Senegal, Seychelles, and Togo. A valid passport (valid at least six months beyond the conference dates) is required. Selected fellows are required to produce at least one piece of investigative journalism inspired by material gathered at the conference, published within three months of the event.
